title: Most consultations decide nothing before you pay
text: In 12 of 19 companies, no medical answer given before sign-in changes the offer. All 42 Hims UK quiz answers led to the same 'Great news'. Hair + Me sold the same unnamed £34.99 treatment to every adult. Boots let nine red flags reach the same screen. A prescriber decides later, after ID, account and card.

title: LloydsPharmacy has the best engine, Numan next, both still blunt
text: LloydsPharmacy removes unsafe medicines on screen for most clinical risks, before sign-in, with prices shown. Numan comes next. Both remove whole drug families silently: any blood-pressure condition removes even the minoxidil spray, and low blood pressure removes topical minoxidil, which the evidence does not require.

title: Red flags rarely stop the sale
text: Patchy, sudden or complete loss should be examined, not treated remotely. Numan, LloydsPharmacy and Dr Fox stop and signpost. Hair + Me, Sons, Strut and the anonymous Hims quizzes do nothing. Boots labels the order 'Danger' for its clinician but still takes ID photos and payment first. (Sons was still in final review.)

title: Mental health handled badly at both ends
text: Numan and Sons show no crisis help for suicidal or hopeless thoughts, and Numan skips the question after a recent dose change. Superdrug's men's form has no mood question. Treated and Philip Kingsley over-block, stopping minoxidil too. The MHRA says ask, discuss and review regularly before finasteride, not block.

title: Safety rules have bugs and bypasses
text: A typo means Philip Kingsley's rule never removes minoxidil for uncontrolled blood pressure. Numan's product links skip its safety filter. Dr Fox lets two consultations put its finasteride spray and finasteride tablets in one basket. Numan and Dr Fox let people change a stopping answer and carry on.

title: Nobody diagnoses properly before prescribing
text: No UK company uses scalp photos to diagnose every new patient; Superdrug asks only for unusual patterns. Only Oxford Online Pharmacy offers blood tests (women; seen in documents only). Nobody asks what happened 2 to 4 months before the shedding, or about weight-loss injections, a listed cause of hair loss.

title: Same finasteride tablet costs up to four times more
text: Licensed finasteride costs £7.25 to £14 a month at Dr Fox and Oxford Online Pharmacy, against about £22 to £35 at Numan, Sons, Hims UK, Treated, LloydsPharmacy, Boots and Superdrug. Headline prices at Voy, Sons and Hair + Me are first-order offers. Hair + Me bills every 4 weeks: £37.91 a calendar month.

title: Unlicensed and extra-strength products lead the subscription ranges
text: Sons, Voy and Hair + Me supply oral minoxidil as unlicensed capsules though licensed tablets exist; MHRA guidance says licensed first. Voy, Numan, Hims and Happy Head sell minoxidil above 5%, though the one trial of 10% found it worse. Happy Head, Keeps and Ro default to their strongest or dearest product.

title: Women are badly served in the UK
text: Six of 12 UK companies (Sons, Numan, Treated, Dr Fox, Boots, LloydsPharmacy) treat men only. The only anti-androgen is Hers UK's fixed 44 mg spironolactone capsule, which cannot be stepped up. No UK women's pathway acts on periods, PCOS, menopause or contraception, and Superdrug keeps Regaine for Women on offer in pregnancy.

title: Cancelling is the top complaint, and the law is changing
text: Cancelling and unwanted renewals appear in 35% of negative reviews (Happy Head 51%, Sons 45%, Keeps 38%). Cheap prices need long prepaid plans; Hims UK cancels only through support. UK subscription rules (reminders, easy exit) are expected from 1 January 2027. A monthly-by-default, easy-exit service would stand out.
